previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, ulcerative colitis, asthma, and a history of DVT/PE was admitted for her 11th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the treatment well, with expected transaminitis that resolved and manageable nausea. An MRI showed stable disease with no evidence of progression. She reported ongoing depressive symptoms, leading to a psychiatry consultation, initiation of citalopram, and referral for outpatient therapy. Social work was engaged to address financial stressors and disability resources. Her chronic right foot pain was reassessed, and gabapentin was uptitrated for better nocturnal control. She cleared methotrexate adequately and was discharged home in stable condition with plans to continue enoxaparin, resume mesalamine, and follow up with oncology in one month for the next cycle.
